metadata.value: Dataset × prediction target; species, tracks, conditions and protocols are linked variants.

A project must primarily develop a substantial, reusable, standardized evaluation framework or benchmark suite for nucleotide/genomic models. Require documented evaluation or software use by at least two distinct external research groups. Citations, surveys, stars, downloads, model adapters, and author-run leaderboards alone do not establish adoption. Shared benchmark authorship does not count as independent adoption. Qualification is not a quality endorsement; adoption is specific to the release and subset actually used.

sources.title: DNAIntelligenceIndex dataset access check

sources.title: GPN-Star published Hugging Face collection

model_properties.name: Corpus
model_properties.value: OpenGenome2: 8.84T nucleotides; eukaryotic and prokaryotic genomes, metagenomes, mRNA, ncRNA, promoters, organelle DNA and splice sites. Official Evo2 preprocessing reported.
model_properties.notes: Source coverage and sampling are reported, not independently reconstructed. This does not establish benchmark decontamination.

model_properties.name: Architecture
model_properties.value: Encoder-only bidirectional Transformer; pre-LayerNorm, RoPE, RMSNorm with zero-centered gamma, SwiGLU. MoE replaces FFNs: 8 routed experts + 1 shared expert, sigmoid routing with learned bias, top-2 routed experts, normalized gate combination.

model_properties.name: Parameter variants
model_properties.value: Small 235M; medium 470M; large 1B total sparse parameters. Active parameters per token, layer counts and hidden widths are unresolved.

model_properties.name: Objective
model_properties.value: Masked-token recovery; no assay labels in pretraining. Load balancing, router z-loss and initial token dropping reported.

model_properties.name: Tokenizer
model_properties.value: Not specified in the inspected report; no public model-specific tokenizer/config established.
model_properties.notes: Do not substitute AIDO.DNA predecessor tokenization or infer one nucleotide per token from the objective.

model_properties.name: Pretraining context
model_properties.value: Progressive 2K → 8K → 64K → 256K schedule; final medium/large 64K, small 256K.

model_properties.name: Consumed tokens
model_properties.value: Embedding diagnostic uses large-8K-4T, explicitly described as 4T consumed tokens. Other model-specific totals remain unresolved.

model_properties.name: Coverage adaptation context
model_properties.value: 524-kb input with frozen backbone and Flashzoi adapter; local sliding-window attention ±8,192 tokens. This is an adaptation/inference procedure, separate from 64K/256K pretraining contexts.

model_properties.name: Corpus sources
model_properties.value: GTDB R220: 67,525 representative genomes; public human-associated prokaryotes: 102,986; in-house gut MAGs: 89,320; UHGV phages: 57,514. Approximately 1.2T nucleotide tokens; 186 phyla, 3,448 families, 69,056 species. Human-associated prokaryote subset: 45 phyla, 585 families, 12,273 species.
model_properties.notes: Corpus/sampling size reported, not independently reconstructed. In-house genomes are not established as public artifacts; downstream holdouts do not establish exclusion from pretraining.

model_properties.name: Sampling
model_properties.value: GTDB: 379B tokens (31.30% dataloader weight); public prokaryotes: 446B (36.85%); in-house gut MAGs: 382B (31.53%); UHGV: 3.8B (0.32%).

model_properties.name: Quality and preprocessing
model_properties.value: Per-context dynamic stratified sampling; prokaryote completeness >90%, contamination <1%; phage CheckV complete or high-quality >90%. Contigs separated with #; runs of >3 N replaced with @; reverse-complement probability 0.5.

model_properties.name: Architecture
model_properties.value: Causal MoE Transformer: 12 layers, width 1024, 16 attention heads, 8 KV groups; 32 experts, top-2/token, expert FFN width 4096; RMSNorm, RoPE base 50M, SwiGLU. 4.7B total parameters, ~330M active.

model_properties.name: Objective
model_properties.value: Next-token prediction; N and unknown tokens excluded from the language-model loss.

model_properties.name: Training context
model_properties.value: 8K→32K→128K→1M bp curriculum; separate sampling schemes at each stage. Exact per-stage token budgets unresolved.

model_properties.name: Optimization
model_properties.value: AdamW, cosine decay, 5% warmup, peak LR 1e-4, gradient clip 1, weight decay 0.1, global batch 1,024, microbatch 1; load-balancing and z-loss coefficients 1e-3; BF16 with FP32 sensitive operations; Megatron parallelism.
model_properties.notes: The released 8K launch script specifies microbatch 4 and no validation iterations; it is a separate artifact from the paper recipe.

model_properties.name: Inference and genome pooling
model_properties.value: Reported 1-Mbp input on one 80-GB GPU; approximately 200 kb on a 24-GB GPU. Whole bacterial genomes are split into 1-Mbp chunks; token embeddings are averaged within chunks and chunk embeddings averaged per genome.
model_properties.notes: No direct same-checkpoint context ablation or retrieval benchmark established. Genome size can exceed a single model context.

model_properties.name: Released tokenizer
model_properties.value: Unigram JSON with 17 listed entries, including single-character C, G, T, A, N, U, #, @ and special symbols. Paper/card report a vocabulary size of 128; released config vocab_size is 256.
model_properties.notes: Keep biological tokenization, listed tokenizer entries and model vocabulary padding distinct; the reason for 128 versus 256 is unresolved.

model_properties.name: Released checkpoint configuration
model_properties.value: MixtralForCausalLM; max_position_embeddings=1,048,576; sliding_window=null; vocab_size=256; router_aux_loss_coef=0.01. Architecture widths and 32/top-2 experts match the paper.
model_properties.notes: The paper/training script auxiliary-loss coefficient 0.001 differs from released inference config 0.01; the inference config alone does not establish the training recipe.

model_properties.name: Released training script
model_properties.value: Script seq_length=8,192, max positions=1,048,576, SentencePieceTokenizer, microbatch 4. This launcher alone does not reproduce 32K/128K/1M training stages.

model_properties.name: RNAfitness cohort
model_properties.value: Thirteen explicit RNAGym assays; 54,384 mutants total. Includes 11 protein-coding assays and 2 ribozymes; no per-assay count inferred from this aggregate.

model_properties.name: Architecture
model_properties.value: Caduceus with Mamba2 blocks; bidirectional processing with shared projections and reverse-complement equivariance. Single-nucleotide masked-token objective.

model_properties.name: Released large configuration
model_properties.value: 48 layers; d_model=1,536; bidirectional_strategy=add; bidirectional_weight_tie=true; rcps=true; vocab_size=8.

model_properties.name: Model sizes
model_properties.value: Small 88M (24 layers, width 768); medium 311M (48 layers, width 1024); large 676M (48 layers, width 1536) in summary/checkpoint labeling. Results/Figure 1 also describe 694M for large.
model_properties.notes: Keep the published discrepancy explicit; no independent tensor parameter count performed.

model_properties.name: Corpus and sampling
model_properties.value: 65 angiosperm genomes from Phytozome; one representative per genus. Gene-centered ±5 kb intervals tiled into 8,192 bp windows with 4,096 bp step; repeats downweighted to 0.1 in MLM loss.

model_properties.name: Tokenizer
model_properties.value: Single-nucleotide tokenization; released config vocabulary size 8 and explicit complementary base mapping. No k-mer segmentation.

model_properties.name: Pretraining procedure
model_properties.value: 240,000 steps; global batch 2,048; length 8,192 bp; 15% BERT-style masking (80% MASK /10% random /10% unchanged); AdamW, cosine decay 2e-4→4e-6, 6% warmup, weight decay 1e-5.

model_properties.name: Context protocols
model_properties.value: Pretrained at 8,192 bp. Conservation comparisons vary centered inputs 512–8,192 bp. Accessibility context experiment keeps 600 bp target labels while extending flanks to 4,600 bp; expression varies 1–4 kb upstream and downstream.

model_properties.name: Supervised adaptation
model_properties.value: LoRA rank 8, alpha 32, dropout 0.1 in x_proj/in_proj/out_proj, plus task readout. One epoch, LR 1e-4, global batch 128; more than 98% of parameters frozen.

model_properties.name: GeneCAD: 2025 paper
model_properties.value: Frozen PlantCAD2 Small/Large encoder; projected contextual states plus token embeddings; trained eight-layer ModernBERT head and 17-class BILOU output; chromosome-wide CRF and protein plausibility filtering.

model_properties.name: GeneCAD: 2026 release
model_properties.value: Full adaptation of emarro/pcad2-200M-cnet-baseline at pinned revision 5574ff5d: backbone not frozen, eight-layer head, 256-dimensional token embedding, 8,192-bp windows. 1,753 updates, effective batch 384, LR 2e-4 cosine schedule.

model_properties.name: GeneCAD training and validation
model_properties.value: Eight training species; random window split within configured chromosomes. Arabidopsis, rice and wheat provide validation windows. 671,523 training and 14,317 validation windows reported; held-out species evaluated separately.
model_properties.notes: Overlapping neighboring windows need not be independent. Source code does not establish chromosome-held-out validation.

model_properties.name: Architecture / tokenization
model_properties.value: 32-layer dilated residual CNN in the 10k architecture; one-hot bases, not learned subword tokens. Position-aligned donor/acceptor/neither softmax; ensemble of five replicas.

model_properties.name: Supervised source and partitions
model_properties.value: GENCODE V24lift37/hg19 principal coding transcripts; chromosome and paralog-filtered reference test. Variant model additionally uses frequent GTEx junctions; evaluation variants occur in ≤4 individuals.

model_properties.name: Context protocol
model_properties.value: 80/400/2,000/10,000 total flanking bases; 40/200/1,000/5,000 each side. 5,000-base central outputs during training; 15,000-base input for SpliceAI-10k. Separately trained context architectures are compared; this is not a same-weights inference-length ablation or a 10-kb maximum gene length.

model_properties.name: Architecture / tokenization
model_properties.value: Approximately 13M parameters; 20 MetaFormer blocks, 256 channels, dilated depthwise convolutions, pooling/upsampling. One-hot bases plus ten species channels; pairwise RoPE attention heads. Graph/path decoder on top of site/junction logits.

model_properties.name: Supervised training corpus
model_properties.value: 314,745 short-read samples from ten mammals plus 330 long-read human/mouse samples. No self-supervised genomic pretraining stage is reported. Gene filtering, intron-chain merging and label normalization matter.

model_properties.name: Base-model context and outputs
model_properties.value: 196,608-bp input; central 65,536-bp site outputs; top 1,024 candidate positions for pairwise junctions. Two-model ensemble. The 200-kb input does not imply a 200-kb fully scored output.

model_properties.name: Transcript benchmark scope
model_properties.value: 352 human genes on chr21/22; human-only training arms. Dominant multi-exon transcript exact splice-pattern match across first-to-last junction ±10 bp. Neither all-isoform recall nor start/end accuracy is established.

model_properties.name: Tissue-conditioned protocol
model_properties.value: 147 RBP expression inputs; 48 tissues; full fine-tuning with 1-kb flanks and capped 64-kb sequence inputs. Different chromosome partition and inference interface from the main model.

model_properties.name: Release inspection limits
model_properties.value: Pinned source code and public checkpoint tree inspected; gated weights and full RNA-seq benchmark labels were not downloaded. Do not promote paper benchmark totals to measured file counts.

model_properties.name: Usage target transformations
model_properties.value: Short-read site/junction targets are normalized by the gene maximum donor/acceptor count and cube-root transformed. Long-read transcript counts are normalized within gene. These are different target definitions, not interchangeable PSI measurements.

evidence.locator: Methods: Pretraining data curation and corpus design; Supplementary Figure1

evidence.locator: Methods: Inference hardware and performance; Discussion

RefSeq CDS, pseudogene, tRNA, rRNA, ncRNA and intergenic fragments; approximately balanced 30k. Documentation says 10-fold cross-validation; inventory gives 9:1. Ten-fold cross-validation per task prose; exact train/validation subdivision unresolved.

CARD positive genes versus length-distribution-matched RefSeq non-AMR genes; single-gene annotation, not strain AST. Project states 8:2 train/test but also ~14.5k train + 1.6k test of 16.1k (approximately 9:1); unresolved.

4,570 VFDB core positive genes; 4,989 DEG essential negative genes after filtering virulence-associated annotations; negatives species-stratified. 8:2 label-stratified random train/test; genus/homology separation not established.
Eight GenerAnno/FitnessBrowser conditions; MSE training loss, Pearson metric. Gene fitness under the specified nutrient/stress condition; not unconditional organism-wide fitness.

MIBiG4 positives excluding fungal, unknown and abnormal-length entries; antiSMASH-screened BGC-free negatives matched on length and CDS count. Given candidate regions, not genome-wide boundary detection.

GIDEON/BacBench 1,175 genomes; independent phenotype classifiers; genus-disjoint 70/10/20, seeds 1,2,3; genome embeddings average 1-Mb chunks. Trait-specific label availability differs.

SAE trained on approximately 305k 32K chunks from pretraining corpus, downsampled and shuffled to ~1B token activations; 4096 latents, Batch-TopK 128. E. coli NC000913.3 one-v-rest annotation alignment; Domain F1 threshold sweep.

Caduceus with Mamba2 blocks, bidirectional shared projections, reverse-complement equivariance; single-base tokens; 8,192 bp masked-LM training, 15% masking; 240k steps, global batch 2048, AdamW with cosine schedule 2e-4→4e-6, 6% warmup, weight decay 1e-5.

65 Phytozome angiosperm genomes; one assembly/haplotype selection, one genus representative; gene-centered±5 kb regions,8,192 bp windows,4,096 bp stride. Methods do not establish chromosome/homology-separated pretraining splits.
Pinned large checkpoint:48 layers, d_model 1536, bidirectional/add, weighttie, rcps=true, vocab_size 8; model type caduceus; context not encoded as max_position_embeddings.
Three model sizes; large reported both 676M and 694M in the published article.
Repetitive nucleotide MLM loss weights 0.1; non-repetitive 1.0. This differs from downstream task sampling.

Actual context experiments: conservation 512–8192 bp; accessibility 600–4600 bp with fixed 600 bp labels; expression 1–4 kb upstream/downstream. Distinguish these controlled input comparisons from a genome-size claim.

Pinned dataset manifest has 12 configs and 20 species/configsplit combinations; card provides sizes for 10 configs and prose for Andropogoneae/SV. Recovery files omit labels; classification files provide binary labels.
Pinned supervised release has 7 configs; counts are manifest-reported unless separately inspected. Cell-type labels serialized as strings; gene-expression files carry genome and orthogroup metadata.

Sorghum reference aligned with 34 other Andropogoneae; >=34/35 coverage; identity>=34 conserved,<15 neutral. Poaceae codingMSA325 genomes; phyloP>5 conserved,<1.5 neutral; intermediates excluded. Each target at 1-based 4096 of 8192 bp.
Score is predicted probability of the actual reference nucleotide; AUROC, not token accuracy.

Maize 26NA Mgenomes:core presentall 26, dispensable 2–23/private 1; tomato 586 accessions:coreall 586, dispensable 6–580/private<5. Uncovered frequency bins not resolved. Canonical maize transcript, longest tomato transcript.

Mask full annotated motif, retain canonical and noncanonical junctions; exact top 1 motifmatch. Maize in pretraining, tomato absent.8,192 bp centered inputs; causal comparators evaluated forward and RC.
Motif accuracy requires every canonical A/C/G/T position correct; groups containing ambiguous symbols excluded. Token accuracy separate.
Core/non-core score is arithmetic mean of true-base probabilities across simultaneously masked motif positions; not an allelicLLR.

Simulated Arabidopsis deletions; negative Delta logP boundary scores versus MSA63 genomephyloP/phastCons constraint proxies; not measured deleteriousness. Mainlabels 7662 conserved/10413 less conserved; flank scoring ablation saturates near 20 nt.

Unmasked ref/mut nucleotide probabilities; negative mean log(mut/ref) at flanks around deletion boundaries. The CLI defaults to five flanking positions per side. This controls output-score averaging rather than truncating the encoder input; the paper flank-width experiment is separate.

Potato SNP constraint labels from 95 Solanaceae-genome GERP:>1.5 conserved,<0 neutral. Solanaceae absent from PlantCAD2 pretraining. FigS3 stratifies CDS, upstream, downstream, intron, intergenic, TE.
Held-out pretraining test sequences:15%random-mask accuracy; central-mask context ablation 512→8192; repeated regions inflate MLM accuracy. Exact coordinate/split generation not established.

Pinned leaderboard stores 220 score rows across 20 species-specific entries and 11 model labels. Context length and selected Evo 2 orientation are per-result fields; this release includes comparators beyond the original journal tables.

Twenty leaderboard entries map to 12 released dataset/target configurations: eight maize/tomato reconstruction entries, eight core-membership entries, three conservation cohorts and one deletion cohort.
Overall ranking averages within-task percentile ranks. It is not a raw-score average; model contexts differ. Evo 2 rows retain a selected strand per task.

LoRA rank 8, alpha 32, dropout 0.1; target x_proj/in_proj/out_proj; over 98% parameters frozen. One epoch, LR1e-4, global batch 128, BF16, linear schedule with 50 warmup steps; no hyperparameter tuning reported.
Released PEFT configuration: rank 8, alpha 32, dropout 0.1, x_proj/in_proj/out_proj. Do not interpret the paper’s generic transformer-attention wording as the actual Mamba2 adapter placement.
Binary classification uses positive softmax scores; PR metric is sklearn average precision. Multilabel PR/AUROC use micro averaging; regression includes Spearman, Pearson, R2, MAE, MSE.

600 bp ATAC peak-centered positives versus remaining genomic background; Arabidopsis chromosome validation and 10 test species; nine-species training holds out maize/barley. Cell-type task:92 maize outputs, held-outchr 10; context variants preserve corelabels.

15 Andropogoneae species panel; validation Tripsacum zopilotense and Zea diploperennis; test 26 maize NAM genomes. TPM >1 expressed,≤1 not expressed; regression log 10 TPM. Inputs concatenate promoter/terminator windows.

Arabidopsis and maize Ribo-seq filtered for rRNA and mapped to genomes; StringTie gene-level ribosome profiling abundance. log 10 abundance regression andTPM>1 binary labels, not direct protein quantitation.
PaperFigureS14 computes within-orthogroup NAM expression correlations; these are lower than across-gene correlations.
Additional maximum-across-tissues expression target and Arabidopsis→maize expression-transfer experiment; neither has a matching named configuration in the seven-config HF release.

evidence.locator: Materials and Methods: Independent Test Set; Model Architecture; Training; Performance Evaluation Metrics
evidence.statement: Five training references: Arabidopsis, soybean, barley, rice, poplar. Five primary test species: walnut, coffee, common bean, N. sylvestris, N. tabacum; maize separate. Frozen PlantCAD2 + projected states/token embeddings +8-layer ModernBERT +BILOU head +chromosome CRF; ReelProtein filter. Full annotation and custom CDS exact matching.

2026 revision: eight training species; U/B/M/R conditions, seeds 11/22/33; defaultMseed 11. Backbone emarro/pcad2-200M-cnet-baseline at 5574ff5d; 1,753 steps, effective batch 384, LR2e-4. Distinct from the 2025 frozen-backbone paper.

Release explicitly says backbone not frozen; 671,523 training and 14,317 validation windows. Athaliana, Osativa, Taestivum contribute validation. Genome/annotation checksums and gene-selection lists available.
All eight species used in training. Arabidopsis, rice, wheat also provide validation windows; soybean, barley, poplar, Aquilegia, Nymphaea training only.
Release splits window indices randomly within each species/chromosome using a seeded permutation. It does not hold out whole chromosomes for validation.

Eight held-out angiosperms plus maize; six distant genomes(two bryophytes, four green algae); one vertebrate model case. CDS-only default/strict gffcompare metrics, predictions and model versions released. References are not redistributed.
Prediction-file manifest: per-file species, model, uncompressed SHA256 and genes_scored. These are prediction counts, not reference-gene counts.

Pinned gffcompare 0.12.10; default and strict(--strict-match -e 0) modes; no-R/-Q denominator restrictions. Levels Base, Exon, Intron, Intronchain, Transcript, Locus. F1 derived from sensitivity andprecision.

Both reference and prediction converted to CDS-onlyGTF: CDS segments become exons; stop codon extension when present; organelles removed; identical CDS chains within gene collapsed. UTRs ignored; phase is not evaluated by the gffcompare input conversion.
Released table has species×model×mode×level sensitivity, precision, F1 for revised coding-only benchmark.
Six distant-genome coding-only annotation evaluations: Physcomitrium, Marchantia, Klebsormidium, Chlamydomonas, Bathycoccus, Ostreococcus.
Experimental vertebrate backbone/model evaluated on marmoset; 48,403 reference coding transcripts and 76,515 query transcripts; default and strict scores. This is not the plant-trained checkpoint.
Boundary sets are extracted from CDS-only chains; exact coordinate/strand set intersections yield precision, recall, F1 forstart, stop, donor, acceptor. Not full transcript start/end prediction.
Source table reports BUSCO complete, single-copy, duplicated, fragmented, missing percentages and lineage size alongside boundary and ORF statistics.

evidence.locator: Benchmark projects: inclusion and adoption criteria
evidence.statement: A project must primarily develop a substantial, reusable, standardized evaluation framework or benchmark suite for nucleotide/genomic models. Require documented evaluation or software use by at least two distinct external research groups. Citations, surveys, stars, downloads, model adapters, and author-run leaderboards alone do not establish adoption. Shared benchmark authorship does not count as independent adoption. Qualification is not a quality endorsement; adoption is specific to the release and subset actually used.
Related BacBench submission describes a dedicated bacterial benchmark; correspondence to the current release and later publication is not established.

evidence.locator: Record schema; evaluation protocol; task index
evidence.statement: Release supplies only text/label train/test CSVs. Upstream dev/validation splits are excluded. MCC is primary; frozen logistic regression uses five seeds and full/10-shot/1-shot regimes.

evidence.locator: Appendix, Dataset Details: TF-H, TF-M, EMP and species classification
evidence.statement: GUE human and mouse datasets are TF binding, not mouse enhancers. Human negatives match GC; mouse negatives are dinucleotide shuffles. Yeast histone labels, human promoters/splice, and virus/fungi origin classifiers are separate tasks.

evidence.locator: Appendix, Task Composition and Table 3; Epigenomic and Regulatory Element Tasks
evidence.statement: GENEB identifies human, Arabidopsis and bacterial iPro promoter datasets, six named-species 4mC targets, 5mC/6mA targets, six plant lncRNA datasets and cassava transcriptional activity. These descriptions do not supply per-row coordinates or a biochemical label-validation audit.
GENEB reports MCC, accuracy and macro-F1; fits logistic regression on frozen embeddings; each seed samples up to k examples per observed class without replacement for 1/10-shot.

evidence.statement: The evaluator and exact expected dataset revision are public, but the dataset endpoint returned HTTP 401. Reported counts remain model-card counts; raw row, taxon and biological-partition verification is unavailable.
Source BioReason coding test split; one fixed prompt per unique original/mutated sequence pair. Gene names are removed because original wording leaked the pathogenic label.
Every row of BioReason non-SNV test split is retained; original source is wanglab/variant_effect_non_snv.
Generated answer is parsed and classified as benign/pathogenic; invalid answers remain misses. Coordinates/biological grouping cannot be checked without dataset access.

Extract the final DNA answer; count position-wise matches divided by reference length. Missing/short answers lose unmatched positions; extra suffix bases do not lower the per-base score. Length-match accuracy is separate.
Four-choice question with answer_index mapped to A–D; choice scorer and per-subtask accuracy. Aggregate gives the six subtasks equal weight rather than weighting by question count.

Evo 2 supplement A.3.1/A.3.3 reports mutation-likelihood evaluations in this frog. The diagnostic panel has no decomposed task record here.
Evo 2 supplement A.3.1/A.3.3 reports mutation-likelihood evaluations in rhesus macaque. The diagnostic panel has no decomposed task record here.

evidence.statement: Evo 2 supplement A.3.2 reports mutation-likelihood evaluations in these species. The diagnostic panel has no decomposed task record here.

Evo 2 supplement A.3.3 reports mutation-likelihood evaluations in this diatom. The diagnostic panel has no decomposed task record here.
Lycophytes; ferns and horsetails. Vascular tissue without seeds; these branches are distinct from seed plants.
Conifers and other gymnosperms: ovules/seeds not enclosed in ovaries; no flowers. A separate seed-plant branch from angiosperms.

evidence.locator: Coverage context / Additional major eukaryotic lineages
evidence.statement: Amoebozoa; CRuMs; Cryptista; Haptista; Excavata; Provora. No finer task placement is recorded for these PR2 v5 branches.
Red algae, glaucophytes and Picozoa have no species-resolved task rows in this catalogue.
Ranunculales is nested within EUDICOTS in APweb. This bridges the missing intermediate eudicot node in the cached Eschscholzia lineage.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods: architecture; model training and testing; PDF page 17
evidence.statement: Dilated residual convolutional sequence-to-sequence model; one-hot A/C/G/T; 80/400/2,000/10,000 total flanking bases, half on each side. Predict donor/acceptor/neither at every output base; 5,000-base training outputs. Five independently trained replicas are averaged.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods: model training and testing, pp.17–18; PDF page 17
evidence.statement: GENCODE V24lift37 principal protein-coding transcripts, hg19. Training pool: 13,384 genes and 130,796 donor–acceptor pairs on chr2/4/6/8/10–22/X/Y; 10% of training genes randomly held for early stopping. Test: 1,652 genes and 14,289 pairs on chr1/3/5/7/9 after excluding genes with any Ensembl paralog. Variant-analysis model adds GTEx junctions found in at least five individuals, while evaluated variants occur in at most four individuals.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods: model evaluation on lincRNAs; PDF page 18
evidence.statement: Longest-exonic transcript per lincRNA gene; retain transcripts accounting for at least 95% of junction reads and with every junction observed. 781 transcripts, 1,047 junctions; score all transcript positions with donor/acceptor top-k accuracy and PR-AUC. This is an annotation-filtered lincRNA evaluation, not a whole-isoform reconstruction benchmark.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods: exon inclusion; Fig.1c; PDF page 19
evidence.statement: GTEx exon inclusion from flanking and exon-skipping junction counts, excluding first/last GENCODE exons; compare with the larger of donor/acceptor predictions. This scores a value at each known exon, not full transcript structures.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods pp.21–26: GTEx processing, validation, effect size, sensitivity; PDF page 21
evidence.statement: 149 GTEx individuals with WGS and multi-tissue RNA-seq. Autosomal gene-body SNVs observed in at most four people; personalized reference alignments. Gains and losses use distinct private-junction/quantitative criteria and expression/coverage eligibility; only 55% of high-score gains and 44% of high-score losses are ascertainable. Sensitivity truth requires effects at least 0.3 and SNVs within 20 nt of affected sites, excluding essential dinucleotides. Validation, sensitivity and effect-size denominators differ.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods: detection of tissue-specific splice-gain variants; Fig.3c; PDF page 27
evidence.statement: Chi-square test of tissue heterogeneity of observed novel-junction usage in GTEx carriers. SpliceAI is tissue-agnostic; this analysis establishes tissue dependence of variant outcomes and does not evaluate tissue-conditioned model predictions.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods pp.27–28: ExAC and gnomAD; Fig.4; PDF page 27
evidence.statement: ExAC v0.3.1 exonic/near-intronic and gnomAD genomes v2.0.1 deep-intronic singleton versus common-variant depletion analyses. Score bins, variant consequences and gene constraint stratify enrichment. These are population diagnostics, not splice-label or transcript exact-match tests.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods: DDD/ASD cohort and gene enrichment, pp.28–29; Fig.5; PDF page 28
evidence.statement: Published de novo variants in 3,953 ASD, 4,293 DDD probands and 2,073 controls; quality/consequence filtering, scaled burden and gene-level mutation-rate enrichment. Cohorts are not supervised fitting folds.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods pp.29–30: LCL validation; Fig.5f and S6; PDF page 29
evidence.statement: Selected de novo predictions in SSC lymphoblastoid cell lines; gain score >0.5 and loss >0.1, using an earlier model without GTEx novel-junction training. Figure S6 describes 36 selected sites; summary reports 21 of 28 assessable patients validated. These units and ascertainment denominators must not be interchanged.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods pp.19–20: motif perturbation; Fig.S2c,d; PDF page 19
evidence.statement: Insert TACTAAC or GAAGAA at controlled offsets around the 14,289 held-out splice-site pairs and measure changes of site scores. This is a model response experiment, not independently measured splicing for the inserted sequences.

evidence.locator: Methods: inputs, architecture and outputs, pp.20–22; PDF page 20
evidence.statement: Approximately 13M parameters; 20 MetaFormer blocks with depthwise dilated convolutions, pooling/upsampling, 256 channels. One-hot bases plus ten species channels. 196,608-base sense-strand input; dense donor/acceptor usage over central 65,536 bases; pairwise junction logits among top 1,024 predicted sites. RoPE dot-product junction heads and dynamic-programming transcript paths; two-model ensemble.

evidence.locator: Methods: short/long-read RNA-seq, pp.19–20; Fig.1a; PDF page 19
evidence.statement: 314,745 short-read RNA-seq samples and 67,493,026 junctions across human, chimpanzee, baboon, crab-eating/rhesus macaques, cow, sheep, pig, mouse and rat. Long-read data: 189 human and 141 mouse samples; filtered to known protein-coding genes and short-read-supported sites. Intron-chain-equivalent isoforms are merged. Retained long-read sets contain 14,257 human/13,491 mouse genes and 593,157/379,729 transcripts. These totals are source/training resources, not held-out evaluation counts.

evidence.locator: Methods: training; variant prediction, pp.24–26; PDF page 24
evidence.statement: Human chr21/22 held for validation; remaining genes and nonhuman species train the main model. BCE for cube-root-transformed short-read site/junction usage; graph-based transcript distribution loss from long reads. 50 epochs, Muon/AdamW, two replicas. Shared candidate sites across alleles support delta scoring; junction changes are excluded from the reported summary score because they gave no net improvement.

evidence.locator: Methods: top transcript benchmark; Fig.1b,c (PDF pp.11–12); PDF page 28
evidence.statement: 352 human genes on chr21/22; multi-exon, most abundant transcript has at least twice the second transcript’s read support. Exact match only from 10 bp upstream of first splice site to 10 bp downstream of last. Human-only models prevent ortholog leakage for this reference-sequence comparison. Figure 1c includes site-only, site+junction and long-read-supervised arms. Held-out chromosomes are also called validation chromosomes; no independent third test is specified. This is not TSS/TES recovery or recovery/quantification of every isoform.

evidence.locator: Methods: GTEx/GEL GT/AG, pp.28–29; Fig.1d,4g; PDF page 28
evidence.statement: Rare SNVs creating GT/AG dinucleotides; matched personalized-diploid RNA-seq establishes novel-site support. Exclude essential splice variants. GTEx: 4,545 cryptic and 573,967 null variants; GEL: 3,065 cryptic and 1,775,800 null. Detection uses auPRC; quantitative GTEx usage uses only the 4,545 cryptic positives and normalizes novel junction counts by the gene maximum donor/acceptor count. Independent variant observations are not a chromosome-disjoint reference sequence test.

evidence.locator: Methods: GTEx sQTL; Fig.1d; PDF page 29
evidence.statement: GTEx v8 significant variant–junction pairs within 50 bp of either junction end, averaged across significant tissues. Fine-mapped PIP≥0.9 in at least one tissue versus PIP<0.1 in all tissues and |mean effect|<0.5; essential splice variants excluded. 2,385 fine-mapped and 3,824 null variants; auROC classification and Spearman on fine-mapped effect sizes are different targets.

evidence.locator: Methods: OpenSplice MPRA, pp.29–30; Fig.1d; PDF page 29
evidence.statement: 283,121 single-base substitutions across 599 OpenSplice exons. SpliceAI2 delta-PSI is the mean of alternate-minus-reference donor/acceptor usage at the measured exon’s boundaries. Comparator scores are released OpenSplice scores. Spearman against experimental delta-PSI; essential splice variants excluded. BEND’s full intervention set and macro-gene fitting/scoring protocol are separate variants of this dataset × target.

evidence.locator: Methods: tissue architecture/training and junction evaluation, pp.30–32; Fig.2b; PDF page 30
evidence.statement: Full fine-tuning conditions on 147 RBP expression values across 48 GTEx tissues. Input uses 1-kb flanks and capped 64-kb genes/segments, not the 196,608-base base-model protocol. Train chr2/4/6/8/10–22/X; validate chr1/3/5/7/9. Candidate anchor-based junction usages are normalized among partners. Evaluation in genes≤64 kb compares top/bottom 24 tissues per junction, after read/depth filters and logit transforms; 14,712,948 pairwise comparisons, not distinct genes or independent samples.

evidence.locator: Methods pp.32–33: tissue-specific variant effect; Extended Data Fig.4c; PDF page 32
evidence.statement: GTEx variants within 20 bp of splice sites; 24 tissues pooled into ten meta-tissues. Coverage and differential-effect filters. Ridge regression (alpha=1, standardized features) compares measured reference usage alone to reference usage plus predicted alternate probabilities; fivefold cross-validation grouped by chromosome. Tissue-specific model predictions added no benefit in the authors’ comparison.

evidence.locator: Methods: RBP motifs and ISM; Fig.2c, Extended Data4b; PDF page 33
evidence.statement: Motif matches in differentially used junctions; 51-base ISM windows. Select the 400 strongest windows per RBP, then compare mean absolute ISM effects across 48 tissues to RBP expression by OLS. Discovery uses chr1–22 and the same biology guides selection. This is selected-feature interpretation, not an unselected held-out regulatory prediction benchmark.

evidence.locator: Methods: SF3B1 uveal melanoma and MBNL1 myotonic dystrophy, pp.34–35; Fig.2d,e; PDF page 34
evidence.statement: SF3B1: 18 mutant/62 wild-type UVM tumors, two RBP signatures and identical DNA; report held-out-gene junction differences, with cumulative acceptor-spacing/polypyrimidine/branch-point filters. DM1: 44 affected and 11 controls in four signatures (11/15/14/15 biopsies), six condition pairs and read/difference filters. Scores are Pearson on clipped/logit junction-usage differences. Cohort totals are donors/biopsies, not held-out junction counts; fine-tuning partition details beyond the stated held-out genes are not separately specified here.

evidence.locator: Methods: population genetics; Fig.3a–c; PDF page 35
evidence.statement: gnomAD v3.1.2, TOPMed freeze8 and UKB ~450k; absent versus common AF≥0.01% protein-coding gene splice-near SNVs within 30 bp, trinucleotide-matched near 1:1 and excluding essential splice. Percent depletion=(1−1/OR)×100 and score–allele-count Spearman; population proxy, not experimentally verified splicing or transcript labels.

evidence.locator: Methods: UKB proteomics; Fig.3d–f; PDF page 36
evidence.statement: 6,149 rare splice-region variants in 1,656 selected genes; 36,764 participants have plasma protein measurements. Regressed Olink residuals averaged in ≥2 unrelated European-ancestry carriers, exclude co-carried rare coding alleles and essential splice; score nearest canonical splice site, signed loss/gain delta. Pearson with mean carrier protein level; observational variant-level target, not protein sequence or full transcript prediction.

evidence.locator: Methods pp.37–38: disease-panel enrichment; Fig.4a–e; PDF page 37
evidence.statement: GEL: 8,778 probands with <100 confirmed/probable panel genes, with dominant-gene analysis in 7,504. Exclude panel genes with TIER1 diagnosis and specified coding/essential splice consequences. Singleton rare SNVs/indels, phenotype-panel match odds ratio/excess versus ten collision-minimized panel shuffles. Null shuffles are not train/test splits or proof of individual-variant causality.

evidence.locator: Methods pp.38–39: RNA-seq validation; Fig.4f; PDF page 38
evidence.statement: 5,435 GEL probands with WGS/RNA-seq; 47,783,068 called variants, 292,651 with SpliceAI2>0.1; after junction eligibility 41,959 variant–gene pairs. Carrier junction percentile≤5th for loss or≥95th for gain against ≥1,000 coverage-qualified samples. Score-ascertained validation rate, not unselected sensitivity or whole-isoform recovery.

evidence.locator: Methods: competing methods, pp.26–28; PDF page 26
evidence.statement: SpliceAI release1.3.1 modified for position-resolved predictions, five bundled models, no masking, reference/alternate signed deltas at specified effect sites for GTEx/GEL GT/AG, sQTL and UKB. Population/disease analyses instead use standard summaries without masking. AlphaGenome raw composite selected over 40 configurations for average performance across eight evaluations; no held-out score-selection cohort specified. OpenSplice uses released comparator scores.
decode_topk_tx returns k×L exonic/intronic arrays by k-best dynamic programming; no independent TSS/TES prediction head.

Training has separate site, junction and transcript tensors and masks; selects junction candidates from observed site usages at training; graph transcript mask uses top observed transcript endpoints. Species one-hot channels and strand reversal are explicit.
Main training entry point puts only GRCh38 chr21/22 in validation; other assemblies remain in training. This does not itself implement the human-only transcript benchmark arm.
get_delta_scores evaluates dense per-base donor/acceptor probabilities but emits per-variant gain/loss deltas and offsets; variant evaluation is distinct from dense site-label evaluation.

evidence.locator: Public model tree API; two model directories
evidence.statement: Two multispecies checkpoints listed; weights not inspected. Source code and manuscript audited; per-benchmark data manifests, eligibility recounts and exact released human-only/tissue checkpoints are not established by the inspected root tree.
Evo 2 compares supervised SpliceAI on ClinVar and SpliceVarDB. These are external SpliceAI evaluations in the Evo 2 paper, not original SpliceAI 2019 experiments.

evidence.locator: Table1; mutation effect prediction; specialist baseline
evidence.statement: BEND 2.0 compares native SpliceAI outputs on OpenSplice (macro-gene Spearman), separately from frozen linear readouts on foundation-model embeddings.

Conservation/TIS/TTS/splicing use the centre-token embedding and scalar labels. Genomic-region classification pools the central 100 bp of a 512-bp window. Neither is a dense sequence-label output. ATAC profile and total counts are different outputs.
Exon/intron evaluation labels only the midpoint of each sequence and probes forward/reverse representations. Genomic position origin and long input context do not make the assessed output dense.

evidence.locator: Gene annotation: Methods4.4, exact CDS-exon/gene scoring and HMM decoding
evidence.statement: HMM converts per-base state/phase predictions into complete coding transcripts. Exon-level exact interval scoring and whole-gene exact coding-structure scoring are separate targets. Primary reference uses longest isoform and excludes UTRs; alternative-isoform sensitivity is a separate analysis. No full mature transcript or all-isoform abundance benchmark is implied.

Each evaluation window contributes one central 128-bp H3K4me3 signal bin. NTv3 base-resolution output is averaged over that bin; source reports chromosome/experiment correlation. This selected-bin readout differs from scoring an entire output profile per input.

Human routing probes report 72,000/9,000/9,000 position rows per target. Selected layers produce continuous HBB display tracks, but the release does not establish that the scored test rows form a contiguous chromosome-held-out labeling benchmark.

The released HBB demonstration contains 20,000 consecutive rows from chr11:5,220,000–5,240,000, selected as the original figure interval, with no random sampling. This proves dense demonstration output, not independence or contiguous coverage of the classifier test cohort.

SAE feature search uses E. coli NC000913.3 ORF/intergenic/tRNA/rRNA annotations; one-versus-rest Domain F1 after activation-threshold sweeping. No separate annotation validation/test cohort is described. Token-wise alignment is an interpretation analysis, not a supervised held-out dense annotation benchmark.

evidence.locator: Supervised coverage prediction / frozen Flashzoi adapter
evidence.statement: Frozen AIDO.DNA2 representations feed an adapted Flashzoi coverage head on long sequences. Five assays score quantitative coverage; output binning is not specified in the inspected technical report. Do not assume single-base labels from input length or Borzoi ancestry.

Every CDS segment becomes an exon; current Base/Exon/Intron/Intron chain/Transcript/Locus scores all concern coding chains with UTRs omitted. The benchmark distinguishes component coordinates from linked structures, collapses identical coding chains, and normalizes stop codons.

Same predictions are scored at six levels with default gffcompare and --strict-match -e 0. Default intron-chain/transcript matching need not require identical outer boundaries; strict mode tightens them. These protocols are not interchangeable.

evidence.locator: Accuracy assessment levels: base, exon, intron, chain, transcript, locus
evidence.statement: Intron-chain match requires all introns with equal count and exact coordinates, ignoring outer ends. Default transcript matching adds single-exon overlap; strict mode constrains terminal ends. Locus match needs at least one matched transcript, not recovery of every isoform.

Released processing selects canonical donor/acceptor positions per exon and compares each mutant with WT. This reduces dense native scores to exon/variant-level deltas, not an isoform-reconstruction output.
Release declares nine gene labels, one enhancer output, 125 accessibility labels, 18 histone outputs and seven methylation outputs.
Frozen embedding CNN with nine positional class outputs, cross-entropy and MCC; source also offers supervised one-hot baselines.
CNN positional output downsampled to128-bp bins; BCE, positive weight82.86, auPRC; chromosome-fold protocol.

Available label_dict includes a nine-class strand-aware CDS/intron/donor/acceptor/noncoding map in which UTRs are noncoding. Other alternative label maps also exist; presence of those maps does not establish additional released UTR targets.
Frozen reference/alternate embedding cosine distance at a configured embedding index; autoregressive models have only left context. No new supervised variant classifier is fitted.

Paper reports 5,976 gene-centred instances, 1,433–14,000 bp; nine strand-aware exon/intron/donor/acceptor/noncoding labels. GENCODE 44 HAVANA coding genes with transcript support and confidence levels 1 or 2; choose the best-supported isoform, breaking ties randomly. GraphPart/global protein alignments split at 80% mature-protein identity; Table 1 reports 4,780/597/597 train/validation/test. Primary MCC over all bases; no cohort-wide chain exact-match score. AUGUSTUS comparison requires exactly one gene with UTR prediction off. This is dense mixed labeling, not an all-isoform or UTR recovery benchmark.

285 human TSS-centred 100,096-bp windows; 782 binary 128-bp labels per window. CRISPRi-validated enhancer–gene links within 50,048 bp; ABC-only predicted links excluded; multiple enhancers can be positive in a window. Ten chromosome groups for cross-validation; auPRC over labels. Negative/unlabelled bins are not an exhaustive experimentally disproven enhancer set.

2,005,617 supplied 512-bp windows with 125 cell-type accessibility labels, not 125 genomic positions. Test chr1/8/9: 372,153; validation chr2/4: 279,422; remaining training: 1,354,042. Mean per-label AUROC. Released config names GRCh37 for accessibility while gene/other configs name GRCh38; exact coordinate-build verification is not replaced by a blanket assembly assumption.

512-bp windows with 18 ChIP experiment outputs covering 11 histone marks in K562. Training: 420,713; validation: 70,801 on chr2/4; test: 120,567 on chr1/8/9. The output vector indexes experiments, not genome positions; mean per-label AUROC.

959,039 supplied CpG-centred 512-bp windows; seven cell-line WGBS labels. Require at least four reads, ≥90%/<10% methylation and measurements in all seven experiments. Training: 743,095; validation: 109,717 on chr5/9/22; test: 106,227 on chr4/13/19/21. Appendix composition says 19 labels, inconsistent with §3.5/Table 1 and the released seven-output config; do not propagate 19 as a measured target count.

DeepSEA/GRASP expression-associated versus 1000 Genomes background SNVs; fold 0, liftOver and reference-base concordance filters; 512-bp paper context. Table 1 reports 105,263 evaluation variants. Appendix source counts of 98,221 background and 8,000 positive variants must not be silently equated to the filtered total. Whole-cohort embedding-distance AUROC; no additional benchmark fitting.

ClinVar noncoding SNV pathogenicity: 295,495 variants in Table 1. Use 512-bp context and reference/alternate embedding distance, with zero-shot AUROC. Source-specific consequence/review filtering; exact eligibility not independently reconstructed in this follow-up.

5,977 rows; split counts {'train': 4783, 'test': 597, 'valid': 597}; 5,974 unique identifiers; coordinate spans 1,433–13,000 bp. Duplicate IDs: {'ENST00000381401.11': 2, 'ENST00000313871.9': 2, 'ENST00000381180.9': 2}. Cross-split identifier overlap: {'test / train': 0, 'test / valid': 0, 'train / valid': 0}. Does not verify protein homology, nucleotide overlap or label truth.

Does not verify protein homology, nucleotide overlap or label truth.

285 vectors, each with 782 entries; values 0.0/1.0 only; 220,185 negative and 2,685 positive bins, 222,870 total. BED windows all span 100,096 bp and partition chromosomes match the paper. This is dense binary annotation, not a quantitative assay profile.

categories.name: Plant breeding
categories.definition: Prioritize trait-associated genes and alleles for plant breeding and validation.

categories.name: Variant interpretation
categories.definition: Prioritize human disease-associated variants and assess molecular consequences.

categories.name: Genetic target discovery
categories.definition: Connect trait-associated variants to genes and molecular mechanisms.

categories.name: Regulatory-sequence engineering
categories.definition: Predict or select regulatory sequences for desired activity in a specified host or cell context.

categories.name: Gene-therapy research
categories.definition: Evaluate sequence components and edits relevant to controlled expression in target cells.

categories.name: RNA engineering
categories.definition: Predict or select RNA translation, stability, binding, localization and molecular function.

categories.name: Strain engineering
categories.definition: Predict gene function and cellular phenotypes relevant to microbial strain modification.

categories.name: Natural-product discovery
categories.definition: Connect biosynthetic sequences to products, chemical properties and substrates.

categories.name: Protein engineering
categories.definition: Predict experimental consequences of coding variants and enzyme function.

categories.name: Microbial genomics
categories.definition: Interpret microbial genes, genomes and mobile elements.

categories.name: Genome annotation
categories.definition: Locate and classify functional genomic elements.

categories.name: Comparative genomics
categories.definition: Characterize homology, evolutionary relationships and sequence constraint.

categories.name: Model development
categories.definition: Measure sequence modeling, representation or computational properties.

categories.name: Functional prediction
categories.definition: Predict an experimentally measured or annotated property from sequence.
categories.accommodation: A task-specific output/readout and appropriate label supervision or score are needed.

categories.name: Variant-effect prediction
categories.definition: Score the consequence of a specified sequence change.
categories.accommodation: Allele comparison, mutation localization and a declared scoring function are required.

categories.name: Sequence modeling
categories.definition: Predict sequence probabilities, held-out bases or natural continuations.
categories.accommodation: A nucleotide/token probability interface with an explicit token-to-base scoring rule is required.

categories.name: Dense annotation
categories.definition: Annotate biological features across sequence using position-aligned labels, detected elements or decoded structures. The Scored output field distinguishes bases, individual elements and complete chains; a supplied midpoint label or a proteome completeness statistic is insufficient.
categories.accommodation: Position-preserving representations and a localized output head are required.

categories.name: Sequence retrieval
categories.definition: Rank related sequences or cross-modal matches.
categories.accommodation: Comparable embeddings or a retrieval score and query/gallery protocol are required.

categories.name: Generation
categories.definition: Produce nucleotide sequence by sampling, completion or sequence optimization. This parent category includes conditional and unconditional generation; candidate selection and probability-only scoring are separate.
categories.accommodation: A generative decoder, sampling or completion procedure is required.

categories.name: Conditional generation
categories.definition: Generate sequence with a specified prefix, activity or organism condition.
categories.accommodation: A mechanism for prefix or attribute conditioning and a declared sampling procedure is required.

categories.name: Sequence selection
categories.definition: Choose candidates for a specified measured response.
categories.accommodation: An effect predictor and a selection objective/budget are required; a generative model is not necessary.

categories.name: Long-context evaluation
categories.definition: Explicitly evaluate context length, distal dependencies or retrieval over extended inputs.
categories.accommodation: Record input span and intervention; long input alone does not establish a long-range biological dependency.

categories.name: Context-specific prediction
categories.definition: Predict dependence on tissue, cell state, genetic background or assay host.
categories.accommodation: A context input or context-specific heads/readouts and matched labels are required.

categories.name: Genetic interactions
categories.definition: Predict non-additive effects or dependence on another allele.
categories.accommodation: Joint mutation/background modeling and an interaction-specific endpoint are required.

categories.name: Evolutionary inference
categories.definition: Predict constraint, evolutionary relationships or functional enrichment.
categories.accommodation: Record alignments, trees and population information available to the model.

categories.name: Structure prediction
categories.definition: Predict secondary or tertiary molecular structure.
categories.accommodation: A structure/contact output and an explicit structure metric are required.

categories.name: Genes / gene bodies
categories.definition: Gene-level sequence or gene-body context. Does not by itself establish full gene-structure recovery.

categories.name: Coding sequence
categories.definition: Protein-coding sequence, including synonymous and nonsynonymous variants.

categories.name: Exons
categories.definition: Exonic sequence, intervals or labels. Correct exon classification/detection does not establish a complete transcript chain.

categories.name: Introns
categories.definition: Intronic sequence, intervals or labels. Supplied intron windows and recovered intron chains are different evaluations.

categories.name: Splice sites
categories.definition: Donor/acceptor boundary identities or local splice-region effects. Junction pairing and complete isoforms are separate features.

categories.name: 5′ UTR
categories.definition: Untranslated sequence upstream of the translated CDS.

categories.name: 3′ UTR
categories.definition: Untranslated sequence downstream of the translated CDS.

categories.name: Noncoding RNA (broad)
categories.definition: Non-protein-coding RNA without a narrower universal class. Broad ncRNA assignments are not automatically “other than lncRNA/rRNA/tRNA”.

categories.name: lncRNA
categories.definition: Long noncoding RNA.

categories.name: rRNA
categories.definition: Ribosomal RNA.

categories.name: tRNA
categories.definition: Transfer RNA.

categories.name: Ribozymes
categories.definition: Catalytic RNA.

categories.name: Aptamers
categories.definition: Nucleic-acid binding constructs.

categories.name: Mature / reporter mRNA
categories.definition: Mature transcript or reporter sequence as input/construct; does not imply reconstruction of a transcript from genomic DNA.

categories.name: Promoters
categories.definition: Promoter sequence or promoter annotation.

categories.name: Enhancers
categories.definition: Enhancer sequence or enhancer annotation.

categories.name: Regulatory DNA
categories.definition: Regulatory intervals without a narrower universal element assignment.

categories.name: TF binding sites
categories.definition: Transcription-factor binding motifs or intervals.

categories.name: Polyadenylation sites
categories.definition: Polyadenylation sites or associated signal regions.

categories.name: Terminators
categories.definition: Transcription termination regions or experimental terminator constructs.

categories.name: Biosynthetic gene clusters
categories.definition: Multi-gene biosynthetic clusters.

categories.name: Operons
categories.definition: Co-transcribed bacterial gene groups or boundaries.

categories.name: Repeats / transposable elements
categories.definition: Repeated sequence or transposable-element annotations.

categories.name: Broad genomic sequence
categories.definition: Whole-genome or broadly sampled sequence context; does not imply genome-wide validation or coverage of every element.

categories.name: Intergenic DNA
categories.definition: Sequence between annotated genes.

categories.name: Chromatin boundaries
categories.definition: TAD/insulation boundaries and associated genomic intervals.

categories.name: Embedding analysis
categories.definition: Analyze sequence representations using projection, clustering or similarity diagnostics.
categories.accommodation: Requires access to hidden representations; diagnostic geometry need not measure prediction accuracy.

categories.name: Model interpretability
categories.definition: Relate learned hidden features to genomic annotations.
categories.accommodation: Requires token-level activations and a feature/readout analysis; threshold selection is part of the protocol.

categories.name: Microbiome analysis
categories.definition: Analyze microbial communities, sample structure and associations with host phenotype.

categories.name: Translation initiation site
categories.definition: Translation start codon and its genomic context.

categories.name: Translation termination site
categories.definition: Translation stop codon and its genomic context.

categories.name: Unconditional generation
categories.definition: Sample sequence without a biological prefix, target activity or other example-specific inference condition. Task-specific training can still define the model distribution.
categories.accommodation: A generative sampling procedure is required; a start-of-sequence token alone is not a biological condition.

categories.name: Isolated labels / values
categories.definition: A label, scalar or non-positional vector for a supplied sequence, locus, exon or variant. Multiple tissues/classes do not make a genomic position axis.

categories.name: Sampled position labels
categories.definition: Labels or feature alignment evaluated at selected genomic/token positions. Dense display tracks alone do not establish contiguous held-out scoring.

categories.name: Dense labeling
categories.definition: Biological labels evaluated at successive positions across each assessed sequence. Independent base accuracy does not establish valid exon chains.

categories.name: Signal profiles
categories.definition: Quantitative experimental signal indexed by multiple genomic positions or bins across an assessed sequence. Distinct from annotation labels and one pooled interval value.

categories.name: Element / boundary detection
categories.definition: A set of intervals or boundaries scored by coordinate matching. Correct individual elements do not imply a complete valid gene/transcript.

categories.name: Gene / transcript structures
categories.definition: Linked exon, intron or coding structures evaluated jointly. Coding phase, outer boundaries, isoform multiplicity and matching tolerance remain protocol-specific.

categories.name: Pairwise relationships
categories.definition: A supplied pair, edge or condition contrast is scored. Junction or enhancer–gene scores do not themselves reconstruct a complete graph or transcript.

categories.name: Sequence generation / recovery
categories.definition: Nucleotide identities or generated sequence. This output alone is not biological dense annotation; experimental and computational validation differ.

categories.name: Retrieval / selection
categories.definition: Ranking, retrieving or selecting among supplied candidates, including edits. Candidate choice is not new sequence generation.

categories.name: Aggregate / diagnostic analysis
categories.definition: Representation, constraint, enrichment, interpretation, runtime or cohort-level analysis. Positional visualizations are not automatically annotation benchmarks.

categories.name: Unresolved / mixed outputs
categories.definition: The available source does not resolve the individual outputs or their scoring population sufficiently.

categories.name: Transcript structures
categories.definition: Linked spliced transcript or coding-transcript coordinates. Coverage does not imply alternate-isoform recall, abundance, TSS/TES accuracy or UTR inclusion.

categories.name: Splice junctions
categories.definition: Donor–acceptor connections or intron chains; distinct from independent splice-site identity and from complete transcript recovery.

categories.name: Gene / transcript structure prediction
categories.definition: Predict linked gene/transcript coordinates and evaluate the chain or gene jointly; matching scope and tolerance are stated separately.
categories.accommodation: Structured decoding, phase/strand constraints or a splice graph may be required; independent site labels are insufficient.

categories.name: Signal-profile prediction
categories.definition: Predict quantitative signal indexed by genomic positions or bins; a scalar whole-window count is not a signal profile.
categories.accommodation: Position-preserving features and a quantitative track head; binning and central cropping must be retained.

categories.name: Element / boundary detection
categories.definition: Locate a set of genomic elements or boundaries across an assessed sequence, rather than classify only supplied candidates.
categories.accommodation: Position-preserving features or coordinate outputs; exact/tolerant interval matching is explicit.

Pearson with mean carrier protein level; observational variant-level target, not protein sequence or full transcript prediction.

This is an analysis of representations, selection, associations or computation. GEL: 8,778 probands with <100 confirmed/probable panel genes, with dominant-gene analysis in 7,504. Singleton rare SNVs/indels, phenotype-panel match odds ratio/excess versus ten collision-minimized panel shuffles. Null shuffles are not train/test splits or proof of individual-variant causality.

Require at least four reads, ≥90%/<10% methylation and measurements in all seven experiments. Training: 743,095; validation: 109,717 on chr5/9/22; test: 106,227 on chr4/13/19/21. Appendix composition says 19 labels, inconsistent with §3.5/Table 1 and the released seven-output config; do not propagate 19 as a measured target count.

DeepSEA/GRASP expression-associated versus 1000 Genomes background SNVs; fold 0, liftOver and reference-base concordance filters; 512-bp paper context. Table 1 reports 105,263 evaluation variants. Appendix source counts of 98,221 background and 8,000 positive variants must not be silently equated to the filtered total. Whole-cohort embedding-distance AUROC; no additional benchmark fitting.

Use 512-bp context and reference/alternate embedding distance, with zero-shot AUROC. Source-specific consequence/review filtering; exact eligibility not independently reconstructed in this follow-up.

protocols.name: Cell-dependent mutation effect protocol
protocols.model_interface: Frozen sequence embeddings
protocols.split_rule: Five folds group each full element and related backgrounds.

protocols.name: Background-dependent mutation effect protocol
protocols.model_interface: Frozen sequence embeddings
protocols.split_rule: Preserve complete element/background groups in five folds.
protocols.notes: 114 elements; shares readouts with cell-context evaluation.

protocols.name: Single-edit repair selection protocol
protocols.model_interface: Predicted effects from frozen embeddings
protocols.split_rule: Use held-out elements and a fixed one-edit menu; candidate outcomes are used after selection.
protocols.notes: 110 elements. Percentile is neither an effect size nor a success rate.

protocols.name: Cell-selective edit selection protocol
protocols.model_interface: Predicted effects from frozen embeddings
protocols.split_rule: Element holdout; selection without candidate measured outcomes.
protocols.notes: 127 loci; equal locus weighting. Uses pooled counts, distinct from posterior effect targets.

protocols.name: Multi-cell activity profile selection protocol
protocols.model_interface: Frozen sequence embeddings
protocols.split_rule: Fit on 5,246 source constructs; 2,411 candidates separated by sequence family. Exclude 27 source constructs whose families touch candidates.
protocols.notes: Two normalized experimental replicates; gain over intent-matched random selection. Replicate values are descriptive, not a confidence interval.

protocols.name: Tissue-profile identification protocol
protocols.model_interface: Frozen full-context sequence embeddings
protocols.split_rule: 12,146 train genes; 1,350 validation; 5,786 held out, four missing predictions excluded →5,782 scored.
protocols.notes: Reference-forward orientation. Full context required; no held-out-tissue transfer claim.

protocols.name: Original AgroNT / PGB procedure

protocols.name: Original AgroNT / PGB procedure
protocols.model_interface: AgroNT sequence encoder plus IA3 / task head
protocols.fitted_component: Task head and IA3 weights; some tasks unfreeze final layers
protocols.split_rule: Cassava chr17 test; chr9 validation; remaining chromosomes train.
protocols.notes: 1-kb windows centered on PRO-seq intergenic peaks, ≥1 kb from genes. Negatives from the same chromosome, outside PRO-seq peaks and within five GC percentage points.

metrics.name: AUROC
metrics.definition: Area under the receiver operating characteristic curve.

metrics.name: Average precision
metrics.definition: Average precision as implemented by the cited scorer; distinguish from trapezoidal PR area.

metrics.name: AUPRC
metrics.definition: Area under the precision–recall curve; integration convention follows the source.

metrics.name: Accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of correctly classified or recovered targets.

metrics.name: Balanced accuracy
metrics.definition: Mean recall across classes.

metrics.name: MCC
metrics.definition: Matthews correlation coefficient.

metrics.name: F1
metrics.definition: Harmonic mean of precision and recall; aggregation follows the protocol.

metrics.name: Pearson correlation
metrics.definition: Linear association with measured targets.

metrics.name: Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: Rank association with measured targets.

metrics.name: Absolute Spearman correlation
metrics.definition: Absolute rank correlation; sign is discarded.

metrics.name: MSE
metrics.definition: Mean squared prediction error.

metrics.name: R²
metrics.definition: Coefficient of determination.

metrics.name: Recall@10
metrics.definition: Fraction of queries with a relevant item among ten retrieved candidates.

metrics.name: Recall@5
metrics.definition: Recall among five retrieved candidates.

metrics.name: MAP@5
metrics.definition: Mean average precision at rank five.

metrics.name: V-measure
metrics.definition: Homogeneity/completeness score for clustering.

metrics.name: Bits per base
metrics.definition: Base-normalized negative log probability.

metrics.name: Rank percentile
metrics.definition: Rank of a selected candidate among experimentally measured alternatives.

metrics.name: Selection utility
metrics.definition: Task-specific utility of selected measured sequences.

metrics.name: Enrichment
metrics.definition: Ratio/enrichment defined by the cited population-genetic analysis.

metrics.name: Association discoveries
metrics.definition: Significant gene–phenotype associations under the declared multiplicity correction.

metrics.name: Exact match
metrics.definition: Fraction of targets recovered exactly.

metrics.name: NDCG
metrics.definition: Normalized discounted cumulative gain.

metrics.name: Recall@50
metrics.definition: Recall among fifty retrieved candidates.

metrics.name: Recall AUC
metrics.definition: Area under the causal-SNP recall curve; source defines rank/threshold axis.

metrics.name: Jensen–Shannon distance
metrics.definition: Distance between predicted and observed profile distributions.

metrics.name: Normalized profile improvement
metrics.definition: Clipped improvement of profile Jensen–Shannon distance over a uniform profile.

metrics.name: Runtime
metrics.definition: Elapsed inference or evaluation time under a fixed workload.

metrics.name: Cluster assignment agreement
metrics.definition: Fraction of samples whose low-depth cluster assignment agrees with the full-depth reference; cluster-label correspondence must be specified separately.

metrics.name: Precision
metrics.definition: Fraction of predicted positive features matching the reference.

metrics.name: Recall / sensitivity
metrics.definition: Fraction of reference positive features recovered.

metrics.name: Mean absolute error
metrics.definition: Mean absolute deviation of predicted continuous targets.

metrics.name: BUSCO completeness
metrics.definition: Percentage of expected lineage orthologs recovered as complete; not annotation coordinate accuracy.

metrics.name: max(AUROC, 1 − AUROC)
metrics.definition: Direction-invariant AUROC with experimental scores binarized at the assay median; not raw AUROC.

metrics.name: Absolute MCC
metrics.definition: Absolute Matthews correlation after experimental and model scores are independently median-thresholded.

metrics.name: Top-k splice-site accuracy
metrics.definition: Fraction of true sites recovered among k predictions, with k equal to the known number of true sites; donor/acceptor averaged.

metrics.name: RNA validation rate
metrics.definition: Fraction of eligible selected predictions meeting the specified RNA-seq criteria; not unselected sensitivity.

metrics.name: Score / measured-effect trend
metrics.definition: Source score-bin distributions or controlled score changes; no single independent predictive correlation asserted.

metrics.name: Tissue heterogeneity test
metrics.definition: Source chi-square p-value for observed novel-junction usage heterogeneity; not accuracy of a tissue-specific model.

findings.description: A.3.6 calls the viral panel 18 DMS datasets, but its prose enumerates more entries and repeats an HIV-envelope author. Individual viral task identities require the released manifest; no exact viral task count is asserted here.

Likelihood perturbation diagnostics (start codons, genetic codes, codon ramps), sparse-autoencoder feature analyses and individual viral DMS tasks are registered in the original source but are not yet fully expanded here.
Original Evo 2 usage is restricted to DART 1, 2 and 5. Registering DART does not establish that Evo 2 ran tasks 3 or 4.
The code pins HF data revision 0c1dda471ad13c6126c2cd00cb3fa34852e70673. The HF repository head inspected separately is newer; download revision and repository head must remain distinct.
LOAM’s layer-sweep chooses the best layer on the test set. Its score is a retrospective maximum and should be kept separate from the fixed-last-layer result.
A-domain labels combine experimental evidence, structure-derived inference, homology and sequence predictions. Do not describe all substrate labels as experimental.
The card calls this multi-label, but the pinned Parquet contains one scalar integer label per row in {0,1,2}. The released task is represented as multiclass; the terminology discrepancy is retained.
The LOAM EC test set has one example per class and layer selection maximizes test macro-F1. Treat its layer-sweep as a different protocol from a fixed readout.
All 70 fitness assay files are now inspected; RNA secondary/tertiary structure tasks remain separate and have not been expanded. Fitness count must not be used as a structure benchmark count.
NABench metadata includes a BRCA1 coding assay labeled as enhancer. Functional-region assignments require source study/artifact reconciliation before importing the manifest wholesale.

The card groups eight task families; donor/acceptor targets are separate records here. Promoter/terminator leaf and protoplast measurements are conditions, not separate species. Rice accessions likewise must not inflate species counts.

Current source catalogue contains 23 dataset names. This catalogue splits the paired reporter half-life/ribosome-load targets, yielding 24 task records; cell/RBP/condition columns remain variants.
Evo 2 is compared in v2 training-free recovery, variant scoring and embedding diagnostics; it is explicitly excluded from revised-NT fine-tuning. No Evo 2 fine-tuning use is recorded.

The released GENERator script applies shuffled KFold within training data when it needs validation; it does not automatically rebuild the released test split. Paper ten-fold averages and release chromosome-held-out tests must be distinguished.

The 33 Table S5 subtasks include allele/consequence strata and composite fitness panels. This catalogue has not expanded every constituent assay. RegMix uses selected VEP evaluations during mixture development.

BOTANIC-1’s development aggregate uses 22 scalars in nine families. Twelve additional cross-species site metrics remain reported separately; task/condition scalars must not be counted as independent biological datasets.

The standardized NTv3 Benchmark contains 155 tracks across 11 species. Assay-level task expansion is pending its full track manifest. All backbones are fine-tuned with a common 32-kb head; Evo 2 covers five species only, not all eleven.
Main-text DeepD methods expose broad endpoints but not all underlying assay IDs and split construction. Composite panels are explicitly marked; they are not counted as fully decomposed benchmarks.
GPN-Star is alignment-conditioned and uses species-specific trained models. Its six-species results must not be represented as a single model transferring to six unseen species.
The LDLR dependency-map analysis is recorded as an exploratory local case study; it does not establish performance on a general experimental genetic-interaction benchmark.

AIDO.DNA2 coverage uses 524-kb inputs and local attention. Reported pretraining context and inference input size do not establish that performance depends on all distal bases; species/track manifests and correlation definition remain pending.

Genos-m documentation reports 51 genomes and 169,408 genes with 30/10/11 genomes, while the pinned HF artifact inspected for LOAM has 55 genomes and 37/9/9. Release/cohort equivalence has not been established.
Documented 8:2 split conflicts with ~14.5k/1.6k counts (~9:1). Neither is silently converted to exact split counts.

Genos-m Table 9 labels its benchmark checkpoint cpt32k while listing 1M maximum context. The connection between this checkpoint, the final released weights and each BGC input protocol remains unresolved. This is separate from evidence of 1M inference feasibility.

Genos-m microbiome applications use sample-level host metadata and additional pooling or abundance-model training. They do not establish microbial species holdouts, direct host-DNA prediction or cross-chunk genomic dependency learning.

The pinned five-fold split file has 2,315 rows (463/fold), while the domain-instance table has 2,504 rows. The scorer further restricts labels/classes; split-file rows must not be presented as final scored single-label instances.

Methods state 36,668TIS sites(26,653/10,015), whereasTable 1/H Fcard state 36,662(26,650/10,012). Non-TIS methods 183,687 versus card 183,685 also differ. Preserve reported counts and inspected artifact counts separately.

The linked leaderboard has 20 species-specific entries corresponding to 12 dataset/target configurations. Its mean percentile ranking combines different contexts and selected Evo 2 orientations. PlantCAD2.5-L is labeled under development; that label does not establish a public model release.
PaperTable 2 summarizes mean AUPRC across 92 cell types, while results prose and released scorer use micro-averaged precision-recall/average precision. These aggregations must remain distinct.

GeneCAD 2025 preprint uses five species and frozen 88M/large PlantCAD2 encoders. The 2026 release uses eight species and explicitly updates a 200M PlantCAD2-family backbone. Its core benchmark is CDS-only with both default and strict gffcompare scoring; those scores must not be presented as full UTR/transcript annotation accuracy.

The inspected release manifest lists 213 prediction files with declared hashes and prediction counts. Reference annotations are linked to their original sources and are not redistributed. Declared hashes were not independently verified against every GFF file.

Inspected translation train and validation files both contain Arabidopsis chromosomes 1–5. This is not chromosome-held-out validation. The exact gene-selection rule remains unresolved; test contains maize chromosomes 1–10.

The paper describes log10-transformed translation abundance. Every released regression label in train, validation and test instead matches log10(1 + TPM), with maximum absolute error below 7e-15. The catalogue uses the released transformation and retains the paper statement separately.

Inspected translation train and validation files both contain Arabidopsis chromosomes 1–5. This is not chromosome-held-out validation. The exact gene-selection rule remains unresolved; test contains maize chromosomes 1–10.

GUE is version-dependent: the supplied list describes an original 28-dataset/7-category suite, whereas DNABERT-2 arXiv v2 describes 36 datasets across 9 tasks. Existing selective GUE records are retained; neither headline count is treated as complete artifact-audited coverage.

Gene-MTEB README says four clustering tasks in its overview but lists four human-virus and four HMP clustering entries; METAGENE-1 section 5.3 describes eight. Reconcile implementation and actual datasets before task expansion.

Output audit: the 170-entry source manifest describes sequence/variant fitness assays. RNA_TYPE alone does not establish element identity or a positional label axis. Individual assay reconciliation remains incomplete.

Output audit: prophage detection/localization can assess interval recovery, but this registration does not yet establish its exact output tensors, scoring unit or task variants. No dense or complete-structure task is inferred.

Output audit: reference-sequence/variant readouts remain to be decomposed. Genome annotation is described as future work in the inspected workshop paper; do not count a released dense gene-annotation task from that statement.

Output audit: the paper includes chromatin-contact-map and functional-track prediction. A scored contact matrix is distinct from a supplied enhancer–gene edge, a TAD-centred classifier and a one-dimensional signal track. Dataset × target/split decomposition is still pending; no matrix task is invented from the registration.

Output audit: short/long sequence tasks and site annotation require task-specific output/scorer reconciliation. Site annotation alone does not establish full gene-chain recovery. No broad dense or structure assignment is made to this registered collection.

Output audit: sequence classification, individual expression/variant readouts and TAD analysis must retain their actual readout units. Long input or a boundary-related dataset name does not establish contiguous label or contact-map evaluation.

Output audit: metagenomic sequence classification/clustering concerns sequence representations, not dense genomic labels. Its sixteen reported entries still require dataset/target and split reconciliation before individual task records are added.
